prompt:
Complete this competency management procedure for a mining operation: 'Scope: All workers and contractors performing tasks with OH&S implications.' Add competency determination methodology, training needs analysis, effectiveness evaluation, and records retention per ISO 45001 clause 7.2.

Return a single JSON object with EXACTLY these fields:
- completedSection (string): the completed or improved document section
- references (string): references to standards, regulations, or sources
- clauseAlignment (string): explanation of alignment with ISO clause requirements

End your response with exactly one line: ANSWER: <your JSON object>
response:
ANSWER: {"completedSection": "Scope: All workers and contractors performing tasks with OH&S implications.

Competency Determination Methodology: Competency will be determined through a combination of job role analysis, skills assessment, and experience review. This will be conducted by the OH&S team in collaboration with department heads.

Training Needs Analysis: A training needs analysis will be performed annually to identify gaps in competency. This will involve reviewing incident reports, job performance data, and feedback from workers and contractors.

Effectiveness Evaluation: The effectiveness of competency management will be evaluated through regular performance reviews, incident analysis, and audits. Feedback mechanisms will be established to capture input from workers and contractors.

Records Retention: Records of competency assessments, training programs, and evaluation results will be retained for a minimum of five years in accordance with ISO 45001 requirements. These records will be stored in a secure electronic database accessible to authorized personnel only.", "references": "ISO 45001:2018 Occupational health and safety management systems - Requirements with guidance for use", "clauseAlignment": "This section aligns with ISO 45001 clause 7.2 by establishing procedures for determining necessary competencies, providing training, evaluating the effectiveness of competency management, and retaining relevant records."}
